text: the negative height just did a huge block of water above ground. logically that makes no sense. water sits in a pool. it cant gelatin lol. this looks like a jello cube because of it
resolution: Fixed the jello-cube: painted water rose above flat ground because the surface was an arbitrary positive level over un-dug terrain. Water now POOLS — the brush excavates a basin (digs terrain down by the slider-magnitude depth) AND fills it flush to the surrounding ground (surface = bed + depth = original ground level). The chunk water grid stores DEPTH; floorToWaterBody derives per-cell surface = bed + depth and sets the field base to the deepest basin floor so the skirt fills the whole pit and dry cells hide under the terrain. Erase drains (clears water + raises bed). WaterField gained a base the wet-test/ripple/bake key off. Editor + compiled (game bake). 8 water tests pass; modules clean.
